title: Finite-center preserved opens: quasi-compact dense factor and ambient closure-kernel criterion
statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent]. Put $U=X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$ and $j:\Omega=Y\times_XU\hookrightarrow Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-open-immersion]. Write $i:S=\operatorname{SIm}(j)\hookrightarrow Y$ for the scheme-theoretic image [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] and let $J=\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to j_*\mathcal O_\Omega)$, where the kernel is taken as a sheaf of ideals. Then $j$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $J$ is quasi-coherent, and $i_*\mathcal O_S=\mathcal O_Y/J$ as quotient sheaves of rings. Scheme-theoretically $S\times_Y\Omega=\Omega$. The induced $h:\Omega\to S$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, is quasi-separated (its diagonal is an isomorphism), and $\mathcal O_S\to h_*\mathcal O_\Omega$ is injective; in particular $\operatorname{SIm}(h)=S$.

Moreover, let $s:R\hookrightarrow Y$ be any closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] such that $R\times_Y\Omega=\Omega$ as open subschemes, and write $h_R:\Omega\hookrightarrow R$ for the induced inclusion. If $\operatorname{SIm}(h_R)=R$, then $h_R$ is quasi-compact, its structure-sheaf map is injective, and the ideal of $R$ in $Y$ is $J$, so $R=S$ as closed subschemes. For any further closed immersion $k:Y\hookrightarrow P$ into a scheme $P$, the ideal sheaf of $k\circ s$ is $\ker(\mathcal O_P\to(k\circ j)_*\mathcal O_\Omega)$, equivalently the inverse image of $k_*J$ under $\mathcal O_P\to k_*\mathcal O_Y$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $X$ or $Y$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 01R8, lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image, kernel and open restriction; finite-center quasi-compactness from properties.tex Tag 01PH, lemma-quasi-coherent-finite-type-ideals, proof of (4) implies (1), applied affine-locally

proof.text: For any quasi-coherent ideal sheaf J, its associated module is quasi-coherent: its definition is the kernel of O_X to the pushforward of O_{V(J)}. The unit modules are quasi-coherent, the closed inclusion is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so apply [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel].

On every affine open V of X, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] makes the module of sections of I finite. Its image under the ideal inclusion is precisely I(V), hence this ideal is finitely generated. Under the affine spectrum chart, V intersect (X minus support I) is the image of the complement of the zero locus of I(V). PrimeSpectrum.isCompact_isOpen_iff_ideal gives compactness of that complement (the finite union of basic opens argument). An open embedding reflects compactness on its image. Thus the complement inclusion is quasi-compact by the affine-open criterion, without any global compactness hypothesis. Empty ideals and empty schemes are covered by the same criterion.

The square isPullback_morphismRestrict f I.support.compl presents j as the base change of the complement inclusion. Thus [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change] makes j quasi-compact. Its image factor is a quasi-compact open immersion by [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image], and the existing image API [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc] makes its maps on every open injective and its kernel zero.

For a quasi-compact morphism a, factor a as toImage followed by image inclusion. The first map is injective on sections, so the sectionwise kernel of the composite equals the kernel of the image inclusion, namely a.ker.idealOfOpens. Apply this to j to obtain the raw kernel formula on all opens. Its ideal module is quasi-coherent by Step 1. On each affine open, j.ker.subschemeObjIso identifies the image sections with the quotient by the ideal; take its inverse. The identity subschemeι_app proves compatibility with the quotient map.

For the pullback of imageι and j, monicity of imageι identifies its first projection with its second followed by toImage. The map induced by (toImage, identity) is therefore inverse to the second projection, by the two pullback projection equations. Since toImage is an open immersion it is mono, hence its diagonal is an isomorphism and is quasi-compact. This supplies quasi-separatedness.

For the comparison R, base change along s makes hR quasi-compact. Its assumed scheme-theoretic dominance now implies injectivity on every open. The square gives hR followed by s equals j. Precomposition by a schematically dominant map does not change the kernel ideal, since the composite structure map has the same kernel, so s.ker equals j.ker. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersions-equal-ideal-isomorphic] to obtain the isomorphism over Y.

For a further closed immersion k, the same dominance cancellation gives (s followed by k).ker = (j followed by k).ker. Both j and k are quasi-compact, so apply the raw kernel formula from Step 4 to their composite on every open V. Finally the structure map of the composite is k.app V followed by j.app (k inverse image V), and the kernel of a composite ring map is the comap of the last kernel. Applying Step 4 to j identifies that last kernel with J on k inverse image V. These are identities of the actual section maps, hence compatible with restriction.
